title: Docs code sample UX: copy behavior, line wrapping, and language tab defaults (streaming pages)
creator: Wei Chen
content:
Context
- As part of the streaming/tool calling examples refresh, we’re updating the streaming guide pages and standardizing code samples across languages.
- Support and DevEx have flagged friction points: (1) copy button copies the wrong thing / fails silently, (2) long streaming loops wrap unpredictably and break copy/paste, and (3) code tabs default inconsistently (users land on TS even when reading Python docs).
- This ticket covers design guidance + interaction specs for docs code blocks and tabbed code samples. Implementation is owned by docs engineering, but design needs to lock conventions so examples are reliable and consistent.

Goals
1) Copy button behavior is predictable, accessible, and copies exactly the active code snippet.
2) Long lines (common in streaming event loops / JSON schema examples) are readable without breaking formatting.
3) Language tab defaults match user intent and persist across navigation.

Non-goals
- Re-architecting the docs site framework or reworking the code renderer beyond the behaviors below.
- Changing API semantics in examples (this is presentation/UX only).

Problems observed (from audit + support)
- Copy button sometimes copies the entire code group (all tabs) or includes UI artifacts; users paste into editors and get invalid code.
- Wrapping differs between browsers; indentation can appear broken, which is particularly harmful for JSON schema and Go/Python blocks.
- The initial tab selection is inconsistent across pages; users bounce between languages when navigating, increasing time-to-first-success.

Decision summary (final)
A) Copy button
- Copy operates on the currently active tab only (never all tabs).
- Copy strips any UI-only artifacts (line numbers, prompts, “$”, “>>>” if present as decoration). If prompts are intentionally part of the snippet, they must be in the code text and will be copied.
- After clicking Copy, show inline state change “Copied” for ~2 seconds (no toast-only confirmation). Preserve focus and support keyboard interaction.
- Provide an accessible name: aria-label="Copy code" (and "Copied" state announced via aria-live="polite").
- Error case (clipboard blocked): show inline “Copy failed” with a short tooltip message: “Your browser blocked clipboard access. Select and copy manually.”

B) Line wrapping / horizontal scroll
- Default: no-wrap + horizontal scroll for desktop/tablet to preserve exact code formatting (critical for streaming loops and JSON).
- Add a per-snippet Wrap toggle (icon button). Wrap mode uses CSS to preserve indentation and enable breaking long strings sensibly.
- Mobile behavior: default to Wrap = ON when viewport is narrow (to avoid unusable sideways scrolling). Users can toggle Wrap off if they prefer exact columns.
- In wrap mode, ensure indentation remains intact (use white-space: pre-wrap and maintain leading spaces; avoid trimming).

C) Tabbed language selector defaults
- Default language selection priority:
  1. Explicit URL override if present (e.g., ?lang=python).
  2. Persisted user preference in localStorage (e.g., last selected language across docs).
  3. Section context inference (if user is within an SDK section, default to that language; otherwise prefer the most common language for the page).
  4. Fallback: first tab.
- When the preferred language is not available in a given code group, fall back to the first available tab and show a subtle note above the snippet: “Python not available for this example — showing TypeScript.”

Interaction / layout specs
- Copy button placement: top-right inside the code block container, aligned with the first line of code, with a stable hit target (>= 32x32px) and no layout shift when switching between Copy/Copied states.
- Copy button should remain visible on scroll within the code block (sticky within the code container) for long snippets.
- Wrap toggle placement: adjacent to Copy (same control cluster), with a clear icon + tooltip (“Wrap lines”).
- Tabs: keep existing tab style, but ensure the active tab is clearly differentiated (contrast) and keyboard navigable (arrow keys across tabs, tab into content).

Accessibility requirements
- All controls keyboard reachable and operable.
- Visible focus ring for Copy/Wrap and tab buttons.
- Copy status change announced for screen readers (aria-live polite region).
- Color contrast meets WCAG AA for text and controls in both light/dark themes.

Acceptance criteria
- Copy copies only the active tab’s code and pastes cleanly into an editor (no extra tabs, no hidden content).
- Copy state changes without moving the button (no jitter).
- Wrap toggle changes only presentation; copied content is always the underlying canonical code (not visually reflowed text).
- Default tab selection is stable across navigation and respects URL override.
- Mobile: code is readable without forcing horizontal scroll by default.

Deliverables
- Final interaction spec (this ticket) + checklist for docs engineering QA.
- Figma redlines are optional; if requested, provide a lightweight component annotation on the existing docs code block component.

Links
- Related work: ENG-4826 (Docs: update streaming pages)
- Related support issue: INT-3321 (docs code tabs broken / inconsistent)
- Related docs PRs: redwood-docs PR-512 (streaming guide updates), PR-534 (code-tab selector fix)

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should Copy include trailing newline? A: Yes (single trailing newline) to improve terminal/editor paste behavior.
- Q: Should Wrap preference persist? A: Yes, persist per user (localStorage) as a boolean; default differs on mobile vs desktop as described.
comments: 2025-02-06 — Kira Thompson: Drafted initial spec based on streaming page audit. Biggest issue is copy grabbing the entire code group in some browsers; recommending copy active tab only + sticky controls for long snippets.

2025-02-07 — Elliot Price: +1 on copy active tab only. Please make sure we don’t imply prompts are removable by default; if prompts are part of code they should copy. Also need a clear rule for wrap vs scroll so streaming loops don’t look “broken.”

2025-02-10 — Wei Chen: Adding requirement: URL param override (?lang=) for support/troubleshooting links. Also want persisted language preference across docs sessions to reduce friction when navigating between pages.
2025-02-12 — Brian Murphy: Please ensure copy output is exactly what’s in the snippet fixtures (golden tests). Copy must not transform quotes/whitespace; wrap must be presentation-only.

2025-02-14 — Kira Thompson: Updated spec: desktop defaults to no-wrap + horizontal scroll; mobile defaults to wrap on. Added ‘language not available’ fallback message to avoid confusion when a page doesn’t have all languages.

2025-02-18 — Jean-Paul Laurent: This will also help quickstarts; some README code groups embed the same component. Please make sure localStorage keys are namespaced to avoid clashes with other Redwood properties.
2025-02-21 — Kira Thompson: Marking Done. Spec approved by docs leadership; docs engineering will implement alongside PR-534 follow-ups and validate on streaming/tool calling pages.
